steps.label: Amplitude
steps.sub: How strongly the qubit is driven — relates directly to how far it rotates

steps.label: Phase
steps.sub: The axis of rotation on the Bloch sphere

steps.label: Frequency + duration
steps.sub: Must match the transition closely; duration trades off against amplitude

steps.label: Calibrated per qubit
steps.sub: No two physical qubits are identical — a tuned pulse isn't reusable unmodified

steps.label: Gate-level (most users)
steps.sub: Write X, H, CNOT — the compiler maps each to its pre-calibrated default pulse

steps.label: Pulse-level (OpenPulse)
steps.sub: Specify envelope, phase, frequency, timing directly — more work, more fragile

steps.label: Why bother
steps.sub: A provider's default is tuned good-on-average, not optimal for your specific case

eyebrow: A concrete example: the DRAG pulse
code:
Problem: a simple pulse can leak
  population into a higher,
  unwanted energy level

Fix: DRAG (Derivative Removal
  by Adiabatic Gate) adds a small
  correction derived from the
  pulse's own envelope

Result: faster gate, or lower
  error, at the same speed
caption: A real, measurable fidelity gain that comes specifically from shaping the pulse — not from any change to the underlying qubit hardware.
